body.title: Describe floor access as an endorsement weighted by context
body.body:
Corrects one sentence in README.md about access to the common capacity floor.

Before: While resources are scarce, access goes through a queue weighted by context, not through an approval.

After: While the network cannot sustain the floor for everyone, mainly when resources are scarce, access depends on an endorsement that works more like a queue weighted by context, such as each person's need and urgency, than like an approval in itself.

Membership statements are unchanged. Anyone still becomes a member by creating their UID, with no approval step.

body.title: Common floor belongs to every member; membership needs no approval
body.body:
## What changed
- **README, Common Capacity Floor:** "every approved member" becomes "every member". The sentence "Approval as a member has requirements of integration and collaboration" is replaced by: anyone becomes a member by being a person and creating their UID, based on multi-factor biometrics certified by people at first enrolment; there is no approval step. While the network cannot sustain the floor for everyone, access goes through a queue weighted by context (need, urgency), and the floor grows as abundance increases.
- **README, Where this stands:** access to the floor belongs to every member and does not depend on rank, reputation or obedience; while resources are scarce, access goes through a queue weighted by context, not through an approval.
- **component.yml:** "a growing common floor for approved members" becomes "for every member".

## Why
Being a member does not require approval: it requires being a person and creating a UID. The common floor belongs to every member; under scarcity it is a context-weighted queue, not an approval, and it never depends on reputation. What the page already said correctly (independent of reputation, growing with abundance, no automatic income or yield) stays.

Mirrored on drayker.org and drayker.com in their own PRs.

body.title: Align reward and allocation wording and license CC BY 4.0
body.body: The reward is the only transferable kind of reputation (README and contract). Allocation by Dk Global follows the single formula: on matters outside the constitution, within the space it grants, open to well-justified vetoes that oblige review. Removes the Portuguese gloss from the English README. LICENSE now carries the full CC BY 4.0 legal code. last_reviewed updated.

body.title: support: contributing capacity earns the reward
body.body:
## What changes
- **README:** what a member contributes earns the reward, a transferable kind of reputation that can give faster or priority access to resources.
- **component.yml:** "A payment, reward or compensation scheme for running a node" becomes "A cash payment or income for running a node", with the reward named; "Any tradable claim…" becomes "Any claim sold for money, income or financial return…".

## Why
The founder's design rewards those who contribute idle compute, run full nodes or build data centres. The reward is reputation of a specific, transferable kind, not money.

body.title: support: biometrics only through the member's UID
body.body:
## What changes
The non-scope line "Biometric intimacy, unverified fixed rates or automatic eligibility as requirements" becomes "Biometric requirements beyond the member's UID, unverified fixed rates or automatic eligibility as requirements", in the README and in component.yml.

## Why
Membership rests on UID, and UID personhood rests on multi-factor biometrics (draykerdk/uid#7). Support cannot rule out biometrics as such. It can rule out asking for biometric data beyond the UID.

body.title: State the case for the common capacity floor directly
body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: update book chapter references to the 2.7.1 numbering
- docs: remove book citations

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #4, closed when the branch was renamed.

body.title: Write what a support node is, in both tiers
body.body:
## What is delivered
The first description of what a support node is, in both tiers: the authenticated, supervised node the main network relies on, and the light contribution the secondary network accepts without identity.

For each: what it contributes, what it has to guarantee, what it is trusted with, and what happens when it returns a wrong result.

## Why it is needed
The design already says trust here comes from redundancy rather than from reputation — the same work computed at several independent points and compared. But nothing public says what a point is, which makes the guarantee unfalsifiable.

Without this, "decentralized" is a claim about intentions.

## Where to start
The two tiers are the interesting part. Something contributed without any identity still has to be worth trusting under comparison, and saying exactly why is most of the work.

## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/fn/
